usual_baseline: Review and stop plans are the gap. PRN benzodiazepines reviewed within a week in 12/38, half continued over 3 weeks [3435]. Weekly review 0–6% [3620]. Zopiclone within 4 weeks in 27% [3543]. Discharge hypnotic review or stop plan 0% [3492]. Sleep hygiene advice 12.5–36.6%, CBT-I 0% [3272][3671]. Written advice 10.7% [3206].
fix_that_works: Teaching residents at rotation start: PRN on discharge 15% to 0%, all with indication and reducing regimen documented [3537]. Unspecified changes cut zopiclone within 4 weeks from 27% to 83.3% [3543]. Acting on earlier recommendations raised discharge medication review from 0% to 56.25% (66.6% on the original wards) [3492]. Community indication documented 61.65% to 80.8% [3206].
fix_that_fails: Written advice fell from 10.7% to 5.8% across repeated cycles [3206]. Specific discontinuation plans reached only 18.75% [3492]. After the zopiclone fix, stop dates, indications and non-drug measures stayed poorly documented [3543]. Sleep teaching showed gains only on clinician self-report, with no record re-audit [3556].
consultant_advice: Plenty of baseline audits, few with hard re-audit numbers. The consistent failures are weekly review of PRN and a written stop plan at discharge. Audit those, and whether non-drug insomnia care is actually offered, rather than prescribing rates alone.
